A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 26-page FANformer paper, including Sections 1–6, references and Appendices A–K. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original FANformer training, scaling, downstream-task and reasoning results in Section 4, with additional hyperparameter, SFT and ablation results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including FANformer benchmark scores, training curves, reasoning evaluations and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same FANLayer modification, ATF attention computation, multi-head construction and SwiGLU architecture. The equations and architecture pseudocode are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dolma training data, validation suites, commonsense benchmarks, modular-addition and linear-regression tasks, ULogic evaluation, and SFT datasets and benchmarks. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 6–7 and Figure 6, including the Transformer variants, pretrained LLMs, GPT-4 on ULogic, OLMo-1B-SFT and MLP representational-capacity baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D and J retain identical model configurations, training budgets, metrics and evaluation procedures, including the Leave-Square-Out split, ten generations per reasoning test point and ULogic scoring.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations, training-dynamics analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity, reasoning-generalization tests, representational-capacity analysis and logical-reasoning case study are all retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same sampling information and statistical reporting practices. v3 adds no repeated-run or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout. For example, FANformer-1B retains the 65.6 average in Table 1 and 38.2% ULogic accuracy in Table 3; appendix SFT and detailed ablation scores also match.

T1.justification: The group-action definition in Section 2, mathematical formulation, computational-cost derivation in Appendix E and ATF equivalence proposition and proof in Appendix I are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about periodicity modeling, scaling efficiency, downstream performance and rule-based reasoning. No core claim is added, removed or broadened.

C2.justification: Interpretations of training dynamics, activation effects, rule learning and expressivity are identical. Appendix K retains the same limitations concerning pretraining scale, untested attention variants and underexplored periodicity mechanisms.

D1.justification: Implementation and access disclosures match, including p = 0.25, 80 A100 GPUs, optimizer and learning-rate settings, approximately 47,600 GPU hours, and the code/model link. Appendix J supplies the same reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to FAN, FNet and attention variants. No citation or substantive research-positioning change is present.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 17 May 2025 to v3 dated 30 September 2025. The prose, author list, terminology, section order and appendix organization are unchanged; extraction-spacing differences do not indicate rewriting.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and 9 tables retain their designs, captions, numbering and placement. Page layout is preserved; negligible rasterization differences do not constitute a figure, table or layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 retains the same method, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility disclosures and limitations as v2, including the appendices. The updated arXiv stamp and negligible rendering differences provide no meaningful gain or loss in clarity, rigor or evidential support.
